page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by a dedicated 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor under the KVM hypervisor. The instance features 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores with 2 threads per core, combined with 48.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU) and 48 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. Network connectivity is delivered via a 12 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Local disk storage is not included, requiring network-attached storage for persistent volume requirements.

Synthetic benchmark evaluations demonstrate balanced compute performance. Multi-core execution achieves a Passmark CPU score of 29,354.86 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,562.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 129.31 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 63.06 GB/sec for uncached large-block writes. Application tests record 23.57 million Redis SET operations per second and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 123.27 GB/sec. Small-scale LLM text generation using a 135M parameter model reaches 298.93 tokens per second, reflecting strong execution efficiency for light inference tasks.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation prioritizes CPU processing density over large RAM buffers, making memory-intensive in-memory data grids less suitable. Furthermore, reliance on remote block storage introduces network latency dependency for I/O operations. The server is well suited for software compilation, web serving clusters, microservices, batch compute pipelines, and small model AI text generation.
